sections.h2: Where is Attleboro and how big is it?
sections.html:
Attleboro is a city in Bristol County on the Rhode Island line, with 46,461 residents at the 2020 census, its highest count ever.

It covers 27.77 square miles and is shaped like a truncated triangle pointing west. It borders North Attleborough, Mansfield, Norton, Rehoboth, Seekonk, Pawtucket, Cumberland and a short stretch of Central Falls. The Ten Mile River runs through the city, and the high point is Oak Hill, at 249 feet, in the south. Attleboro is part of the Providence metropolitan area and is also linked to Boston.

Attleboro is a patchwork of older mill villages and crossroads, and a listing there usually names the village.

  • City Center, the downtown business district beside the L.G. Balfour Riverwalk
  • South Attleboro, near the Rhode Island border
  • West Attleboro and East Attleboro
  • Hebronville, Dodgeville and Maple Square
  • Briggs Corner, North Corner, Oak Hill, Park Square, East Junction and Camp Hebron

The city also sits on a dialect boundary: the eastern part speaks like Boston and the western part like Providence.

sections.h2: Why is Attleboro called the Jewelry City?
sections.html:
Attleboro was once known as the jewelry capital of the world because of its many manufacturers.

The industry took off in 1913, especially through the L.G. Balfour Company, whose plant site is now a riverfront park. Firms such as Guyot Brothers, which dates to 1904, General Findings, Garlan Chain and Leach & Garner remain in operation. In 2011 the city won $5.4 million in state and federal funding to turn underused industrial and commercial parcels in the historic downtown into mixed-use space and to improve MBTA rail, GATRA bus service and roads.

Check the age of any house before you set expectations. Homes in a city that has been settled since 1634 range widely in age, so heating systems, wiring and roofs deserve a careful look.

sections.h2: How do you get around Attleboro?
sections.html:
Attleboro sits beside Interstate 95, with commuter rail stations and a regional bus system.

  • Highways: Interstate 95 enters the state between Attleboro and Pawtucket, Interstate 295 ends nearby, and US Route 1 and Routes 1A, 118, 123 and 152 cross the city. Routes 118, 123 and 152 meet at the city center.
  • Rail: two MBTA commuter rail stations, one downtown and one in South Attleboro near the Rhode Island line.
  • Bus: the Greater Attleboro Taunton Regional Transit Authority, GATRA, links Attleboro, Taunton and surrounding towns.
  • Air: T.F. Green International Airport in Warwick, Rhode Island, and Boston Logan International Airport.

A house near a rail station or an I-95 ramp appeals to commuters going toward Providence or Boston.

Attleboro Public Schools runs the city's district, with five elementary schools, three middle schools and two high school programs.

The elementary schools are Hill-Roberts, Hyman Fine, A. Irvin Studley, Peter Thacher and Thomas Willett. The middle schools are Brennan, Coelho and Wamsutta. Attleboro High School opened a new building in 2022, following a $260 million project, and Attleboro Community Academy is an evening program for students aged 16 to 25. Bishop Feehan High School is a Catholic school, and Bristol Community College and Bridgewater State University both have satellite sites in the city.

sections.h2: When are Attleboro real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Attleboro's tax bills have four due dates a year: August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1.

If a date lands on a weekend or holiday, the payment is due the following Monday. The city collector's real estate tax page adds some details that surprise people.

  • Unpaid amounts accrue daily interest at 14 percent per year.
  • The city does not accept postmarks as proof of timely payment.
  • Not receiving a bill does not excuse the tax or the interest.
  • Payment can be made online, by phone, by mail, in person at City Hall at 77 Park Street, or at the drop box at the Pine Street entrance.

The collector's page also lists separate pages for municipal lien certificates and tax title, which sellers should consult when a balance is owed.

sections.h2: Who gets the bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
The collector must send the bill to the owner of record as of January 1 of the year the property was assessed.

That means a new owner may not see a bill in their own name for some time after a purchase. The city suggests that new owners contact the Assessor's Office to confirm the right owner details are on file. For a seller, the lesson is to settle taxes through the closing statement rather than assuming a later bill will go to the buyer.

sections.h2: Which dates matter at the Attleboro Assessor's Office?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office, at 77 Park Street, publishes a short calendar of deadlines.

See the city's key dates page. For the steps after an abatement is denied, the Appellate Tax Board's appeals guide gives a three-month window to appeal.

sections.h2: What if an Attleboro tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
The city gets a lien on the property automatically, and a tax taking can follow.

The Land Court's overview says a demand can go out after 30 days of nonpayment, and a taking can be recorded 14 days after that. An owner can still redeem by paying what is owed before the court enters a foreclosure judgment. Selling during that period is one way to pay the balance from proceeds.

sections.h2: What do you need to close a sale in Attleboro?
sections.html:
One state requirement applies to every one or two family home sale: a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance.

The Department of Fire Services guide says to call the local fire department as soon as you have a closing date. Battery-powered smoke alarms older than 10 years, or expired, must be replaced, and the department charges for the inspection. Deeds for an Attleboro property are recorded at the Bristol County Registry of Deeds, which the Assessor's page links for deed searches.

sections.h2: How do Attleboro owners compare listing, selling alone and cash offers?
sections.html:
Each route trades price against speed and effort.

A listing can bring a higher price for a house in good shape. Selling alone saves a commission but puts marketing and negotiation on the owner. A direct cash offer fits a house that needs work, an estate, or an owner who wants a firm closing date. Compare each offer by what you walk away with after taxes, payoffs and repairs.

faqs.q: How many people live in Attleboro, Massachusetts?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 46,461 residents, the highest count in the city's history. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 47,447.

faqs.q: When are Attleboro property taxes due?
faqs.a: August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, payment is due the following Monday.

faqs.q: Does Attleboro accept postmarks for tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The city collector says it does not accept postmarks, so payment has to be received by the due date. Interest accrues daily at 14 percent per year on late amounts.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for an Attleboro abatement application?
faqs.a: February 1. The Assessor's Office lists it as the deadline to apply for a property tax abatement.

faqs.q: Which Attleboro train stations serve commuters?
faqs.a: Attleboro has two MBTA commuter rail stations, one downtown and one in South Attleboro near the Rhode Island line.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Attleboro house with taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Taxes and liens are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so request a written payoff figure from the collector before your closing date.
